topPRs.title: justfile: Auto-select the native or Docker kona prestate build
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Adrian Sutton** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1786315831137179?thread_ts=1786315831.137179&cid=C0BHEH8TG91)_

Follow-up to #22340, which fixed the next failure up the same `just build-deps` chain.

## Before

`just build-deps` from `op-acceptance-tests` runs `just cannon-prestates`, which always took the native MIPS64 cross-compile. That needs the MIPS64 GCC toolchain, which is apt-only — no macOS package provides it — so on a Mac the recipe could never succeed. Adrian, on macOS:

```
error: linker `mips64-linux-gnuabi64-gcc` not found
  |
  = note: No such file or directory (os error 2)

error: could not compile `kona-client` (bin "kona-client") due to 1 previous error
warning: build failed, waiting for other jobs to finish...
error: could not compile `kona-client` (bin "kona-client-int") due to 1 previous error
error: Recipe `build-kona-client-elfs` failed with exit code 101
error: Recipe `build-kona-prestates` failed with exit code 101
error: Recipe `cannon-prestates` failed on line 253 with exit code 101
error: Recipe `build-deps` failed with exit code 101
```

A raw rustc linker error, after cargo has compiled the whole dependency graph, naming nothing to install and not mentioning that the repo already has a Docker build that works fine on macOS.

## After

`just cannon-prestates` (and so `just build-deps`) picks a build that this host can actually run:

- **Linux with the cross toolchain** — unchanged, the fast native build.
- **macOS, or any host without the toolchain** — the reproducible Docker build, which is what CI uses.
- **Neither available** — a message naming what to install for each path, instead of a linker error:

```
error: cannot build the kona prestates: no MIPS64 cross toolchain, and no Docker.

Install either:
  * the MIPS64 cross toolchain, for the native build (apt only, so not macOS;
    provides 'mips64-linux-gnuabi64-gcc'):
      sudo apt install g++-mips64-linux-gnuabi64 libc6-dev-mips64-cross binutils-mips64-linux-gnuabi64
  * Docker, for the reproducible build (the supported path on macOS):
      https://docs.docker.com/get-started/get-docker/

Then re-run, or pin a build with KONA_PRESTATE_BUILD=native|docker.
```

Docker is never used unconditionally — an environment without Docker keeps working exactly as before.

## How

- `cannon-prestates` now calls a new `rust/justfile` recipe `build-kona-prestates-auto`, which probes for the cross-linker on `PATH` and delegates to the existing `build-kona-prestates` (native) or `build-kona-reproducible-prestate` (Docker). Both write the same per-variant artifacts dirs, so consumers cannot tell which ran; only the hashes differ, and only the Docker build's match releases.
- **The Docker path also builds the host `cannon` binary.** The reproducible build builds cannon as a Dockerfile stage and exports only the prestate dirs, but `op-devstack` points the challenger's `VmBin` at `cannon/bin/cannon` (`op-devstack/shared/challenger/challenger.go`), which the native path leaves behind. Without this, the fallback would produce prestates whose tests then fail on a missing cannon. Built before the Docker build so a broken Go toolchain fails fast.
- `build-kona-client-elfs` checks the linker up front, so `cd rust && just build-kona-prestates` (still native-only, as documented) reports a missing toolchain before cargo compiles anything, and points at the Docker recipes as the alternative.
- The toolchain names move into `MIPS64_CC` / `MIPS64_CXX` / `MIPS64_LINKER`, each defaulting to the literal used today and reading the same environment variable the build already exports (`CARGO_TARGET_MIPS64_UNKNOWN_NONE_LINKER`, `CC_mips64_unknown_none`, `CXX_mips64_unknown_none`). So a differently named toolchain is both probed for *and* used — previously the recipe clobbered such an override. `lint-kona-cannon` picks up the same variables instead of repeating the literals.
- **Override:** `KONA_PRESTATE_BUILD=native|docker` pins a path and skips detection. There was no existing override to respect; the name follows the repo's existing env-var convention (`KONA_CUSTOM_CONFIGS_DIR`, `KONA_SYNC_SUPERCHAIN`, `RUST_JIT_BUILD`).
- Docker is probed for the CLI only, not daemon liveness: a stopped daemon already fails with its own actionable error (`Cannot connect to the Docker daemon … Is the docker daemon running?`), and picking a build should not cost a daemon round-trip on machines that never needed Docker.

## CI is unaffected

CI never runs `cannon-prestates`. The `cannon-prestate` jobs in `.circleci/continue/main.yml` and `rust-e2e.yml` run `just reproducible-prestate`, and `rust-ci.yml` runs `just build-kona-reproducible-prestate` — both the Docker path, called directly, and neither goes through the changed recipe. `op-acceptance-tests`' `build-deps` exits early when `$CIRCLECI` is set, so the recipe is only ever exercised on developer machines (the same reason #22340's bug reached `develop`).

Inside the prestate Dockerfile, `build-kona-client-elfs` runs on the `cannon-builder` image, which apt-installs `g++-mips64-linux-gnuabi64` (`rust/kona/docker/cannon/cannon.dockerfile`), so the new preflight passes there. It must already be on `PATH` under exactly that name, since the current build exports it as the linker and succeeds.

## Not a mise problem

Worth stating since it would change the right fix: this toolchain is deliberately *not* managed by mise. `mise.toml` pins no MIPS cross-compiler, and `rust/kona/docker/README.md` documents it as "MIPS64 cross-compilation toolchain (manual, apt only)" — frozen in the `cannon-builder` image precisely because apt versions are not deterministically pinnable. So there is no mise entry to add, and Docker really is the only option on macOS.

## Verified

With the pinned `just` 1.46.0, using a stub `mips64-linux-gnuabi64-gcc` on `PATH` and a stub `just` to observe which recipe is selected:

- Linker present → native build selected.
- Linker absent, Docker present → Docker build selected, preceded by the host cannon build.
- Neither → the error above, exit 1.
- `KONA_PRESTATE_BUILD=docker` with the linker present, and `=native` without it → override wins in both directions. An invalid value is rejected by name.
- `CARGO_TARGET_MIPS64_UNKNOWN_NONE_LINKER=my-custom-mips-gcc` → `MIPS64_LINKER` resolves to it, so the probe and the export agree.
- End-to-end `just cannon-prestates` with no linker reaches the real `docker build`, failing only on this sandbox's absent daemon.
- `build-kona-client-elfs` prints the new preflight error without a linker, and proceeds past it (to `install-nightly`) with the stub present.
- `cd cannon && just cannon` builds `cannon/bin/cannon` successfully on a host with no MIPS toolchain, which is the step the Docker path now adds.
- `just --evaluate` clean on both justfiles; `just --list` entries render correctly.

## Not verified here

- **The real Rust MIPS build and the real Docker build.** The sandbox has no MIPS toolchain and no Docker daemon, and the `op-rs/reth` git dependency is network-blocked, so cargo cannot even resolve dependencies. The native and Docker recipes themselves are unchanged, but the end-to-end macOS run — `just build-deps` picking Docker and producing usable prestates plus a working `cannon` — needs a machine with Docker. @ajsutton, this is the bit to try.
- Whether Docker Desktop's `linux/amd64` emulation makes the fallback slow enough on Apple Silicon to want a warning up front.

topPRs.title: docs(rpc-providers): add SwiftNodes to RPC provider directory
topPRs.author: swiftnodes
topPRs.body:
### Summary

Adds **SwiftNodes** to the Production RPC providers directory.

SwiftNodes is a multi-chain RPC provider offering flat-rate HTTP + WebSocket access. It serves several OP Stack mainnets — **OP Mainnet** (chain ID 10), Base, Zora, Unichain, Fraxtal, Mode, and Soneium — which meets the directory's bar of supporting at least one OP Stack network.

The entry is inserted alphabetically (between RockX and Tenderly) and follows the existing Description / Supported Testnets / Supported Mainnets format. Only capabilities we actually serve are listed (mainnet-only; no testnets).

topPRs.title: justfile: Scope build-rust-release cargo flags with explicit -p
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Adrian Sutton** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1786315831137179?thread_ts=1786315831.137179&cid=C0BHEH8TG91)_

## Before

A developer runs `mise exec -- just build-rust-release` (directly, or via `just build-deps` / `just acceptance-test` from `op-acceptance-tests`) and it dies within a second, before compiling anything:

```
error: no bin target named `op-reth-sdm-fixture` in default-run packages
help: available bin in `op-reth-sdm-fixture` package:
    op-reth-sdm-fixture
```

No Rust binaries get built, so local acceptance tests can't start at all.

## After

The recipe builds all six binaries as intended — `kona-node`, `kona-host`, `op-reth`, `op-reth-sdm-fixture`, `op-rbuilder`, `rollup-boost`.

## How

`rust/Cargo.toml` declares a `default-members` list of four paths:

```toml
default-members = [
  "kona/bin/host",
  "kona/bin/client",
  "kona/bin/node",
  "op-reth/bin/",
]
```

A bare `--bin` is resolved **only** against those default members. `op-reth-sdm-fixture` (`rust/op-reth/crates/sdm-fixture-node/`) is a workspace `members` entry but not a default member, so cargo cannot see its bin target. The other three names in that line (`kona-node`, `kona-host`, `op-reth`) happen to live in default members, which is why only the fixture broke.

The fix pairs `-p` with every `--bin`, matching the two lines directly below it and the `rust-op-reth-binary` CI job, which already builds this binary with `--package op-reth --package op-reth-sdm-fixture`.

**Why not just add `-p op-reth-sdm-fixture`?** Because `-p` narrows package selection for the *whole* cargo invocation, not just the `--bin` that follows it. The one-flag version swaps one breakage for another:

```
$ cargo build --release --bin kona-node --bin kona-host --bin op-reth \
      -p op-reth-sdm-fixture --bin op-reth-sdm-fixture
error: no bin target named `kona-node` in `op-reth-sdm-fixture` package
```

So all four packages have to be named. All four `-p` values were checked against `cargo metadata` — each package name is identical to its bin name.

Broken since #22289 introduced the fixture.

## Why CI didn't catch this

`op-acceptance-tests/justfile` short-circuits `build-deps` in CI, because CircleCI builds these binaries in dedicated jobs and passes them through the workspace:

```bash
build-deps:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    if [[ -n "${CIRCLECI:-}" ]]; then exit 0; fi
```

`build-rust-release` is therefore only ever executed on developer machines, and a green CI run says nothing about whether it works. Confirmed: `CIRCLECI=true just build-deps` exits 0 immediately without running anything.

## Verification

What I confirmed:

- **Reproduced the exact reported error**, and confirmed the fix, against the repo's real package names, real bin targets and real `default-members` list. Sandbox network policy blocks the `op-rs/reth` git dependency (`403` from the proxy on `https://github.com/op-rs/reth`), and cargo resolves the dependency graph *before* target selection — so a real build stops earlier than the bug in this environment. To get past that, I generated a dependency-free mirror of the workspace: all 75 members reproduced with their real `[package] name` and real `[[bin]]` targets from `cargo metadata --no-deps`, stub `main.rs` bodies, and the same `default-members`. Against that mirror:
  - current `develop` flags → `error: no bin target named `op-reth-sdm-fixture` in default-run packages` (verbatim match to the report)
  - one-flag `-p` variant → `error: no bin target named `kona-node` in `op-reth-sdm-fixture` package`
  - this PR's flags → exit 0, producing exactly `kona-host`, `kona-node`, `op-reth`, `op-reth-sdm-fixture`
- All four `-p` names exist as packages, cross-checked against both `cargo metadata` and each `Cargo.toml`'s `[package] name`.
- `justfile` parses under the pinned `just` 1.46.0, and `just --dry-run build-rust-release` emits the intended command.
- Audited every other `--bin` in the repo's justfiles/Makefiles for the same latent bug. All remaining bare `--bin` uses name default-member bins (`kona-node`, `kona-host`, `op-reth`) or live in `rust/rollup-boost`, which declares no `default-members` (so all members are default). `rust/justfile`'s `build-kona-client-elfs` already passes `-p kona-client`. **No other instance of this bug.**

What I could **not** verify: a real end-to-end `env -u CIRCLECI just build-deps`. It is not runnable in this sandbox — `mise` is unavailable and cannot be installed (`mise.run` and GitHub release downloads are both blocked, `403`), and the Rust build's `op-rs/reth` git dependency is blocked by the same policy. Both blockers are environmental and unrelated to this change. **A maintainer should still run `env -u CIRCLECI mise exec -- just build-deps` from `op-acceptance-tests/` once to confirm the full path end to end** — that's the acceptance bar this PR targets, and it's the one step I couldn't execute.
